main.claim: Paste your text, choose a voice, and press play. Your browser reads it aloud with the voices it already has. Change the speed and pitch, pause, resume or stop, and see a character count. Free, no sign-up.

sections.heading: How to hear text read aloud
sections.body:
Open the [text to speech tool](https://text-to-speech.lazur.app/) in your browser. Paste the text you want to hear into the box, choose a voice, and press play.

1. Open [Text to Speech](https://text-to-speech.lazur.app/).
2. Paste or type your text into the box.
3. Choose a voice from the list. The voices are grouped by language.
4. Set the speed and pitch if you want a change.
5. Press play and listen.

**The voice reads your text exactly as you wrote it.** You do not need an account or an app. The page works in your browser, using the voices your browser already has.

sections.heading: Pick a voice and set the pace
sections.body:
The voice list shows the voices your browser can use, grouped by language. Pick one that matches the language of your text. The list depends on your browser and your computer, so a voice you see in one browser may not show up in another. If you want a different voice, try another browser or check which voices your computer has installed.

Two sliders change how the voice sounds. The rate slider sets how fast the voice speaks. The pitch slider sets how high or low it sounds. Move one slider at a time and play a short sentence after each change, so you can hear what it does. For a long text, a slower rate is often easier to follow while you do something else.

sections.heading: Play, pause, resume and stop
sections.body:
Press play to start the voice. Press pause to hold your place, then press resume to carry on from the same spot. Press stop to end the speech.

Use pause when you plan to come back to the same place. Use stop when you are finished with that text.

sections.heading: Check the length and try the sample text
sections.body:
The character count shows how many characters are in the box. Look at it before you listen, so you know how long the text is.

The sample text gives you a passage to try without typing anything. Load it, pick a voice, and press play. Move the sliders while it reads, then paste your own text when you are ready.

sections.heading: What this tool does not do
sections.body:
This tool reads text with the voices your browser has. It does not make AI voices, and its features do not include saving the speech as an audio file. Use the play controls to listen now, while you work or check a draft.

If you write by voice on your Mac, Lazur works the other way round: hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

pages.keyword: text to speech on google docs
pages.title: Text to Speech on Google Docs: Read Your Doc Aloud | Lazur
pages.description: Copy your Google Doc into this text to speech page, choose a voice, and press play. Steps for long documents and what to do when the voice sounds wrong.
pages.h1: Text to speech on Google Docs
pages.claim: This tool does not open Google Docs files. Copy the text from your doc, paste it here, choose a voice, and press play. Free, in your browser, with no sign-up.

sections.heading: Copy your Google Doc into the tool
sections.body:
The tool reads text you paste in. It does not read the file itself, so you move the text across once.

1. Open your document in Google Docs.
2. Select the text you want to hear. To select all, press Ctrl+A on Windows or Cmd+A on a Mac.
3. Copy it with Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on a Mac.
4. Open [Text to Speech](https://text-to-speech.lazur.app/google-docs) in a new tab.
5. Paste the text into the box with Ctrl+V or Cmd+V.
6. Choose a voice and press play.

Your document stays as it is. Copying the text does not change it, and you can go back to Docs at any time to edit.

sections.heading: What Google Docs offers on its own
sections.body:
Google Docs has a screen reader setting in its accessibility options. Google's help page explains that you must turn screen reader support on before you use it, and it lists keyboard shortcuts for reading a selection aloud once that support is on. The help page at [Google Docs accessibility](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/179738) is the place to check the current steps.

That help page does not give a plain step-by-step way to read a whole document aloud, so this page does not repeat menu steps for it. If you want to choose your own voice, set the speed and pitch, and pause in the middle of a document, copy the text into this tool instead.

sections.heading: Long documents, one part at a time
sections.body:
If your document is long, you do not have to paste all of it at once. Copy one section, a few paragraphs, and listen to it. Then pause, and copy the next section when you are ready.

This works well for a report, an essay or notes you want to check. Each part plays in order, so you can keep your place. The character count in the box shows how long the part you pasted is, so you can see when a section is short or long.

sections.heading: When the voice sounds wrong for the text
sections.body:
Text to speech reads what it is given. Symbols, short forms and names can come out strangely. If you hear a word read wrong, change the spelling in the box to how you want it said. Write out abbreviations in full, and add spaces where a line of numbers or symbols runs together.

If the voice sounds flat or hard to follow, pick another voice from the list. Then change the rate slider a little at a time until the speed suits you. Listen to the first paragraph before you press play on the whole text.

sections.heading: Write by voice in Google Docs on your Mac
sections.body: Reading a draft aloud is only half of the work. If you also write in Google Docs by voice, Lazur does that part on a Mac. Hold two keys, talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, including your Doc.

faq.q: Can Google Docs read text aloud?
faq.a: Google Docs has a screen reader setting that can read a selection, but its help page does not give a plain step-by-step way to read a whole document aloud. To hear a doc with a voice you choose, copy the text into this text to speech tool, pick a voice, and press play.

faq.q: How do I get Google Docs to talk to me?
faq.a: Select the text in your doc and copy it with Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on a Mac. Paste it into the box on the text to speech page, choose a voice, and press play. You can pause, resume or stop at any time.

faq.q: Does the tool open my Google Docs files directly?
faq.a: No. This tool does not open or connect to Google Docs, so you paste the text in yourself. Your document is not changed when you copy from it.

pages.title: Text to Speech on Mac: Built-In Option and a Free Tool | Lazur
pages.description: Read text aloud on a Mac with the built-in Option-Esc shortcut, or paste text into this browser tool. Set up the Mac feature, pick a voice and listen.
pages.claim: Turn on Speak selection in System Settings, then press Option-Esc to hear highlighted text in most apps. Or open this tool in Safari or Chrome, paste your text, and press play. Free, no sign-up.

sections.heading: Turn on the built-in Mac feature
sections.body:
Your Mac can read selected text in most apps. Apple's steps, as they are on its help page, are below.

1. Choose Apple menu, then System Settings.
2. Click Accessibility in the sidebar. You may need to scroll down.
3. Click Read & Speak.
4. Turn on Speak selection.
5. Select the text you want to hear, then press Option-Esc.
6. Press Option-Esc again to stop.

The full guide is at [Have your Mac speak text that is on the screen](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/have-your-mac-speak-text-thats-on-the-screen-mh27448/mac).

sections.heading: Use this tool in Safari or Chrome
sections.body:
If you want to paste text and control the speech with buttons, use this tool. It runs in your browser, so you do not install anything.

1. Open [Text to Speech for Mac](https://text-to-speech.lazur.app/mac) in Safari or Chrome.
2. Paste your text into the box.
3. Choose a voice from the list. The voices are grouped by language.
4. Move the rate slider for speed and the pitch slider for tone.
5. Press play. Use pause, resume and stop as you need them.

The voices you see depend on your browser and your Mac. If a voice you want is missing, try the other browser and check which voices your Mac has installed.

sections.heading: Built-in shortcut or this tool: which to use
sections.body:
Use the Option-Esc shortcut when you are reading in an app and want to hear a passage without leaving it. Highlight the text, press the shortcut, and listen.

Use this tool when you already have the text in front of you and want more control. You can paste a long passage, see the character count, use the sample text to test a voice, and pause in the middle and come back to the same place.

sections.heading: If nothing plays
sections.body:
If the built-in shortcut does nothing, check that Speak selection is still on in Read & Speak. Make sure some text is highlighted before you press Option-Esc, and check the volume on your Mac.

If this tool stays silent, check the volume and the output device on your Mac, choose a voice from the list, and press play again. If the list is empty, open the page in the other browser and try again. The voices come from your browser, so a browser with no voices installed cannot read the text.

sections.heading: What this tool does and does not do
sections.body:
This tool reads text with the voices your browser has. It does not make AI voices, and its features do not include saving the speech as an audio file. Use the play controls to listen while you work or check a draft.

If you dictate on your Mac, Lazur is the other half of this. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.q: Does a Mac have built-in text to speech?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on Speak selection in System Settings under Accessibility, then Read & Speak. Select text in most apps and press Option-Esc to hear it. Press Option-Esc again to stop.

faq.q: How do I turn off text to speech on a Mac?
faq.a: Press Option-Esc to stop speech that has already started. To turn the feature off, open System Settings, go to Accessibility, click Read & Speak, and turn off Speak selection.

faq.q: Can I use text to speech in Safari on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes. Open the tool in Safari or Chrome, paste your text, choose a voice, and press play. The voices you see depend on your browser and your Mac, so check the list if a voice is missing.
